sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setting up the web page
sections.what: Adds the project folder to the import path, loads the libraries for data, charts, maps and the web page, and sets the page title and layout from config.
sections.why: The page must set its basic look before anything else is drawn.
sections.watch_out: The page setup call must run before any other Streamlit drawing command, so code placed above it will cause errors.

sections.name: load_data (part 1)
sections.title: Querying events with filters
sections.what: Builds a database query that joins events to their projects and applies the time window, sector, subsector, country, stage, capex, and impact filters.
sections.why: Lets the page show only the events the user selects.
sections.watch_out: The join is an inner join, so events with no linked project never appear.

sections.name: load_data (part 2)
sections.title: Running the query and returning a table
sections.what: Runs the query, sorts the results newest first, and returns them as a table, or an empty table when nothing matches.
sections.why: A table is easy for the cards, totals, and map to read.
sections.watch_out: Nothing here caches results, so each change in the sidebar reruns the database queries.

sections.name: get_unique_values
sections.title: Getting dropdown choices from the database
sections.what: Returns a sorted list of distinct values for sector, subsector, country, or stage, to fill the sidebar menus.
sections.why: Keeps the menus in step with what is actually in the data.
sections.watch_out: An unknown column name returns an empty list silently, so a typo gives an empty menu.

sections.name: get_event_stakeholders
sections.title: Looking up stakeholders for one event
sections.what: Returns the stakeholder rows for one event as simple records with role, name, ticker, and confidence.
sections.why: Event cards need the stakeholder details in a simple form.
sections.watch_out: This runs one database query for each event card shown, which can be slow when many events are listed.

sections.name: create_map (part 1)
sections.title: Preparing the map points
sections.what: Checks there is data with coordinates, colours each point by impact (red high, orange medium, green low), sets each point size from its money amount, and builds the map layer and starting view.
sections.why: Likely reason: colour shows importance at a glance, and size is meant to show money.
sections.watch_out: The size formula appears to have its minimum and maximum reversed, so almost every point ends up the same size, unless the amount is very large.

sections.name: create_map (part 2)
sections.title: Drawing the map and tooltip
sections.what: Draws the map with a tooltip that shows the project name, event title, impact, and money, then renders it on the page.
sections.why: Lets a reader hover over a point to see its details.
sections.watch_out: The map style is a Mapbox style, which normally needs an access token, and none is set in this code, so the base map may not load. The tooltip money field uses Python number formatting inside a template, which may show raw text instead.

sections.name: display_event_card
sections.title: Drawing one event card
sections.what: Draws an expandable card with the project name, short summary, impact and confidence figures, money in millions, stage, up to five stakeholders, and up to three source links.
sections.why: Gives the detail behind each map point and list entry.
sections.watch_out: The card formats impact and confidence as numbers, so a value that is empty rather than a number can break the card.

sections.name: main (part 1)
sections.title: Drawing the sidebar filters
sections.what: Shows the page title and builds the sidebar with a days slider, dropdowns for sector, subsector, country, and stage, capex range boxes, and an impact slider.
sections.why: Gives the user controls to narrow the events shown.
sections.watch_out: The subsector list shows every subsector from all sectors, even though a comment says it depends on the chosen sector, so picking a subsector from another sector returns no events.

sections.name: main (part 2)
sections.title: Showing totals, map, and event list
sections.what: Loads events for the chosen filters, shows four totals (events, total money in billions, average impact, number of projects), draws the map, and lists event cards with the highest impact first.
sections.why: Gives an overview first, then the detail.
sections.watch_out: The capex range boxes treat 0 as no limit, so a real limit of zero cannot be set.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Starting the page when run directly
sections.what: Runs the main page function when this file is started as a script.
sections.why: A standard Python pattern, and Streamlit also runs the file this way.

summary: A Streamlit web page that shows capital project news events with filters, totals, a world map, and expandable event cards.
purpose: Lets a reader explore recent events by sector, country, stage, size, and impact.
why: Likely reason: an interactive page makes the stored events usable without writing database queries.
how: 1) Set the page title. 2) Build sidebar filters, with choices taken from the database. 3) Query events using the filters. 4) Show four totals. 5) Draw the map from events with coordinates. 6) List event cards sorted by impact.
inputs: Database rows from the event and project tables, the sidebar choices, and the page title and layout settings from config.
outputs: A web page with totals, a map, and event cards.
risks: Zero in the capex boxes means no limit. The map style may need an access token. Map point sizes are effectively uniform. Each card runs its own database query, and nothing is cached. Empty values can break a card.
debug: If the page is blank or shows an error, check the terminal running Streamlit for a traceback. If totals look wrong, check the filters first, then query the database directly. If cards fail, look at the card function. If the map is empty, check that the project records have latitude and longitude.
